text:
A prominent anti-vaccine and ketamine-therapy advocate. His name? Gavin de Becker.
 
And who was he wining and dining aboard his luxury yacht in Greece?
 
That would be our nation's Secretary of Health and Human Services, Robert F. Kennedy Jr.
 
According to The Wall Street Journal, Kennedy received more than $250,000 in gifts from de Becker, a major political donor and longtime associate. Those gifts included expensive flights to Greece and Fiji and the use of a home in Washington, D.C.
 
And now we're learning that Kennedy ALSO vacationed aboard de Becker's 151-foot luxury yacht in Greece.
 
That yacht trip? NOT included in his federal ethics disclosure.
 
Now, here's where things get interesting.
 
The Wall Street Journal lays it out well: “Federal ethics rules generally prohibit executive branch officials from accepting gifts from individuals with interests in their official responsibilities. There is an exception for gifts from personal friends.”
 
Kennedy and de Becker say they're personal friends and that these gifts have nothing to do with Kennedy's government work.
We're talking about a major political donor who advocates for positions on vaccines and ketamine therapy, issues that fall squarely within the responsibilities of the very department Kennedy leads.
 
And we're supposed to just take their word that there's nothing to see here?
 
The American people deserve to know whether the Secretary of Health and Human Services is making decisions in the public interest or whether wealthy donors with interests in his department are receiving special access.
 
Public service is supposed to be about serving the American people, NOT enjoying luxury vacations courtesy of wealthy political benefactors.
 
Congress needs to get to the bottom of this. No one should be above accountability.
